en.name: Repetition mark (踊り字)
en.note: Repeats the preceding kanji; the second part is often voiced.

en.name: Small vowels
en.note: Form a new sound together with the preceding character, mainly in loanwords (see extended katakana).

en.name: Sokuon (促音)
en.note: Small tsu: the following consonant is doubled – you pause briefly before it.

en.name: Historical kana (wi, we)
en.note: Replaced by い and え since the 1946 script reform; today you only see them in names and brands.

en.name: Chōonpu (長音符)
en.note: Lengthens the preceding vowel, almost only in katakana. In hiragana the long vowel is written out.
